answer: Reputation-decayed entry pricing. Each new identity must post a fee that rises with recent arrival rate in its subnet, so a burst of registrations pushes marginal cost up sharply before it can settle into a stable haven. A zephyr of organic growth costs little; a coordinated swarm pays steeply per head. Fees decay only after sustained independent activity, so abandoned identities forfeit their value and cannot form a cheap nebula of dormant accounts.
